description: Rules for MDX tutorial content quality, structure, and consistency.

rules.title: No skip-ahead directives in body
rules.description: Do not include 'Non-technical readers: skip ahead...' text in lesson body. The 🟢/🔷 badges on section headings already communicate audience clearly in mixed tutorials. Skip-ahead text is redundant clutter.

examples.bad: *Non-technical readers: skip ahead to the [Concept Check](#concept-check) below.*
examples.good: (Omit the line entirely. The 🔷 badge on the heading is sufficient in mixed-audience tracks.)

rules.title: Audience badges on section headings (mixed-audience only)
rules.description: For mixed-audience lessons, every ## section heading must start with either 🟢 (Core — for everyone) or 🔷 (Technical — for developers). This rule does NOT apply to pure-technical lessons where no audience distinction is required.

examples.bad: ## 3. System Prompt Syntax Across Models (in mixed-audience lesson)
examples.good: ## 🔷 3. System Prompt Syntax Across Models (or no badge if pure-technical lesson)

rules.title: Lesson roadmap table required (mixed-audience only)
rules.description: Each mixed-audience lesson file must have a '📍 Lesson Roadmap' blockquote near the top containing a table mapping sections to audience. This is omitted for pure-technical lessons.

examples.good:
> **📍 Lesson Roadmap:**
> | Section | Audience |
> |:---|:---|
> | 1. Topic Name | 🟢 Everyone |
> | 2. API Details | 🔷 Technical |

rules.title: Concept Check must use checkbox syntax
rules.description: Quiz options in Concept Check sections must use the checkbox syntax `* [ ]` for wrong answers and `* [x]` for the correct answer. Do NOT use plain bullet points for quiz options.

detection.pattern: Lines under a '## Concept Check' heading should match `* \[[ x]\]` pattern
